data.title: A Lightweight Approach to FDOs via Bioschemas, RO-Crate and Signposting on GitHub Pages
data.abstractNote: Here we present a proof-of-concept using Bioschemas, RO-Crate and Signposting as a lightweight approach to FDOs describing research outcomes exposed on GitHub pages. Research artifacts produced by a research and development team, namely the SemTec team at ZB MED, are exposed via GitHub pages and enriched with structured metadata using schema.org and Bioschemas. Research artifacts corresponding to the same research project are put together in an RO-Crate. Signposting is used on the GitHub landing pages. The combination of these three elements facilitates rich FAIR metadata for research artifacts.

data.abstractNote:
The team of participants from the German National Library of Medicine (ZB MED - Information Centre for Life Sciences) applied FAIR Signposting and RO-Crate to the team’s web pages as a proof-of-concept for later developments. The team web pages now support FAIR Signposting and RO-Crate for projects and theses, with the next step being implementation for software.

data.title: Usage guidance (aka profiles) for the machine-actionable Software Management Plan Ontology
data.abstractNote: Usage guidance (aka profiles) including suggestions of mimimum, recommended and optional properties as well as property cardinality for the metadata schema/ontology maSMP (published at DOI:10.5281/zenodo.7806638, vr. 2.1.0). Although this is the first publicatoin of profiles separated from the metadata schema, we have decided to keep a relation in the versioning of the schema and the profiles, therefore these profiles correspond to vr. 2.1.1. These profiles are mostly based on the SMP metadata crosswalks from May 2023 and December 2023, and correspond to the types OuputManagementPlan, SoftwareManagementPlan, SoftwareRunAction and SoftwareTestAction defined in the maSMP metadata schema, and to the types schema:SoftwareApplication and schema:SoftwareSourceCode so the proposed properties for these two types are covered. The maSMP types and maSMP profiles can be visualized in the Data Discovery Engine (DDE) platform. Follow the links and you will get a summary of types and properties, and the corresponding profiles with usage guidelines (e.g., minimum, recommended and optional properties with cardinality). The profiles include recommendations on types and properties from: schema.org v23 Codemeta Bioschemas maSMP vr. 2.1.0 Acknowledgments  This project received funding (December 2022 to May 2023) from the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme under grant agreement No 101017536 which is part of the Research Data Alliance and European Open Science Cloud Future call 2022. More info.   The maSMP project is part of the NFDI4DataScience project funded by the German Research Foundation (DFG), project number 460234259.

data.title: Synthetic data: how could it be used in infectious disease research?
Synthetic data: How could it be used for infectious disease research?
data.abstractNote: Over the last three to five years, it has become possible to generate machine learning synthetic data for healthcare-related uses. However, concerns have been raised about potential negative factors associated with the possibilities of artificial dataset generation. These include the potential misuse of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in fields such as cybercrime, the use of deepfakes and fake news to deceive or manipulate, and displacement of human jobs across various market sectors. Here, we consider both current and future positive advances and possibilities with synthetic datasets. Synthetic data offers significant benefits, particularly in data privacy, research, in balancing datasets and reducing bias in machine learning models. Generative AI is an artificial intelligence genre capable of creating text, images, video or other data using generative models. The recent explosion of interest in GenAI was heralded by the invention and speedy move to use of large language models (LLM). These computational models are able to achieve general-purpose language generation and other natural language processing tasks and are based on transformer architectures, which made an evolutionary leap from previous neural network architectures. Fuelled by the advent of improved GenAI techniques and wide scale usage, this is surely the time to consider how synthetic data can be used to advance infectious disease research. In this commentary we aim to create an overview of the current and future position of synthetic data in infectious disease research.

machine-actionable Software Management Plan Ontology (maSMP Ontology)
data.abstractNote: We have defined a metadata schema in the form of an ontology representing the necessary metadata elements for a maSMP. The metadata schema includes entities involved in software management planning; such as an SMP itself, software source code, software release, documentation, authors and their relations. We are reusing terms mainly from schema.org and from the RDA-DMP-Common-Standard maDMP application profile, with some few additions of our own.   Vr.2.1.0 is better aligned to schema.org (i.e., use of schema:domainIncludes and schema:rangeIncludes). It includes four types: OuputManagementPlan, SoftwareManagementPlan, SoftwareRunAction and SoftwareTestAction, and additional properties for schema:CreativeWork, schema:SoftwareApplication and schema:SoftwareSourceCode.   The maSMP types and maSMP profiles (published at DOI:10.5281/zenodo.10582121) can be visualized in the Data Discovery Engine (DDE) platform. Follow the links and you will get a summary of types and properties, and the corresponding profiles with usage guidelines (e.g., minimum, recommended and optional properties with cardinality).   The schema is based on: schema.org v23 Codemeta Bioschemas ELIXIR SMP SMP metadata crosswalks from May 2023 and December 2023 RDA-DMP-Common-Standard maDMP application profile DataCite vr 4.4, particularly the description of output management plans Acknowledgments  This project received funding (December 2022 to May 2023) from the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme under grant agreement No 101017536 which is part of the Research Data Alliance and European Open Science Cloud Future call 2022. More info.   The maSMP project is part of the NFDI4DataScience project funded by the German Research Foundation (DFG), project number 460234259.

data.title: Results from aligning the maSMP metadata schema to the RSMD guidelines
data.abstractNote:
Here we report on our final presentation and results from our aligning the machine-actionable Software Metadata Plan (maSMP) metadata schema to the Research Software MetaData (RSMD) guidelines. This activity was carried out as part of the FAIR-IMPACT support action to implement the RSDM guidelines and was identified with the ID OC-RSMD-11.

The RSMD guidelines target metadata providers for them to offer quality metadata while our maSMP supports structured metadata. To align them both, we worked with a spreadsheet, listing all the RSMD guidelines and then identifying the related types and properties from our types. 

This report includes the following files:



Alignment of maSMP metadata schema to RSMD.tsv --a tab separated values file corresponding to the alignment assessment between our maSMP metadata schema and the RSMD guidelines.

OC-RSMD-11-final-slides.pptx --slides presented during the last workshop of the action call in PPTX format

OC-RSMD-11-final-slides.odp --slides presented during the last workshop of the action call in ODP format

OC-RSMD-11-final-slides.pdf --slides presented during the last workshop of the action call in PDF format


Acknowledgements

The first version of the maSMP metadata schema was created thanks to funding from the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme under grant agreement No 101017536, part of the Research Data Alliance and European Open Science Cloud Future call 2022. 

Since June 2023, the maSMP project has been part of the NFDI4DataScience project funded by the German Research Foundation (DFG), project number 460234259. 

The FAIR-Impact support action calls has received funding from the European Commission, grant “FAIR-IMPACT – Expanding FAIR Solutions across EOSC” number 101057344. The alignment activities reported here were carried out within the scope of the FAIR-Impact support action call for “Implementing the Research Software MetaData (RSMD) guidelines for better archiving, referencing, describing, and citing research software artefacts”, mentored by Morane Gruenpeter and Sabrina Grainger from the Software Heritage Foundation.

data.title: Enriched BERT Embeddings for Scholarly Publication Classification
data.abstractNote: With the rapid expansion of academic literature and the proliferation of preprints, researchers face growing challenges in manually organizing and labeling large volumes of articles. The NSLP 2024 FoRC Shared Task I addresses this challenge organized as a competition. The goal is to develop a classifier capable of predicting one of 123 predefined classes from the Open Research Knowledge Graph (ORKG) taxonomy of research fields for a given article.This paper presents our results. Initially, we enrich the dataset (containing English scholarly articles sourced from ORKG and arXiv), then leverage different pre-trained language Models (PLMs), specifically BERT, and explore their efficacy in transfer learning for this downstream task. Our experiments encompass feature-based and fine-tuned transfer learning approaches using diverse PLMs, optimized for scientific tasks, including SciBERT, SciNCL, and SPECTER2. We conduct hyperparameter tuning and investigate the impact of data augmentation from bibliographic databases such as OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, and Crossref. Our results demonstrate that fine-tuning pre-trained models substantially enhances classification performance, with SPECTER2 emerging as the most accurate model. Moreover, enriching the dataset with additional metadata improves classification outcomes significantly, especially when integrating information from S2AG, OpenAlex and Crossref. Our best-performing approach achieves a weighted F1-score of 0.7415. Overall, our study contributes to the advancement of reliable automated systems for scholarly publication categorization, offering a potential solution to the laborious manual curation process, thereby facilitating researchers in efficiently locating relevant resources.

BioHackEU23 report: Enabling FAIR Digital Objects with RO-Crate, Signposting and Bioschemas
data.abstractNote: As part of the BioHackathon Europe 2023, we here report from the progress of the hackathon project #15: "Enabling FAIR Digital Objects with RO-Crate, Signposting and Bioschemas". We added Signposting to three existing resources, and made a Chrome browser extension to show Signposting headers. We added RO-Crate to two existing resources, and explored making a hybrid FDO using both a Handle PID Record and Signposting/RO-Crate approach.
